lines.pro_contract_after.01:
Kahaha! My eye is open at last!
…Hmm. The whole world
looks like a feast.
lines.pro_contract_after.02:
…What are you eyeing?
Don't eat my sword.
lines.pro_contract_after.03:
That toothpick?
Not to my taste, two-bit adventurer.
lines.pro_contract_after.04:
As the contract says: your life is mine.
You shall not die without my leave.
In return, I eat all that you cut down.
lines.mech_forecast.01:
Now you'll see it too.
The number over each monster's head.
The blood you'll shed in that fight.
lines.mech_forecast.02:
There's no luck in it. No dice.
If the number changes, so did you.
lines.mech_forecast.03:
So that number
is the thing's price.
…You've got a merchant's eye.
lines.mech_forecast.04: From now on, I'll ask. How much?
lines.mech_forecast.05:
Do I look like a merchant?!
The price floats over their heads,
two-bit adventurer!
lines.mech_forecast.06:
…If you must know, open the book.
Whatever's left on this floor,
my eye has priced it all in there.
lines.mech_crit.01:
Kahaha, watch closely.
The next one, I cut in earnest.
lines.mech_crit.02:
In earnest? You mean a critical hit?
Luck?
lines.mech_crit.03:
Luck, my hilt. I count the breaths.
On a set count, one cut is in earnest.
lines.mech_crit.04:
The breaths I count carry over,
even after the fight ends.
So who you cut first sets the price.
lines.pro_kingslime_reveal.01: King? The only king here is this blade!
lines.pro_kingslime_reveal.02:
…Sniff, sniff.
That blob over there
reeks of my magic.
lines.pro_kingslime_reveal.03:
Of all the vermin in that forest,
that one gnawed me the most!
lines.pro_kingslime_reveal.05:
Revenge? Kahaha, it's a meal!
I'm eating back what they stole.
lines.pro_kingslime_reveal.06:
I'll lend you Smash, Bulwark, Drain.
Hit hard, block, heal by what you cut.
Each one, once per fight.
lines.pro_kingslime_reveal.07:
The number doesn't count those three.
Slot them in well, and it gets cheaper.
lines.pro_kingslime_reveal.08:
…So I could finish
for less than the number.
lines.pro_kingslime_clear.01:
Kahaha! See that, two-bit adventurer?
Three at once, still just the number.
Look at the numbers first. Fear later.
lines.pro_kingslime_clear.02:
…Not a price worth fearing.
From now on, numbers first.
lines.pro_kingslime_clear.03:
Now then, my turn.
Mace, dagger, shield…
By contract, every one is mine!
lines.pro_kingslime_clear.05:
…The contract said weapons too.
So you really do eat them.
lines.pro_kingslime_clear.07:
In the dark…
I was looking up at a black sun.
lines.pro_kingslime_clear.09:
…I don't know.
It came back to me as I ate.
lines.pro_kingslime_clear.10:
…A warm belly…
makes the eyelid… heavy…
…*mumble*.
lines.village_card.01:
Past the forest, it came into view:
a black tower, planted upside down
in the heart of the village.
lines.village_card.02:
One night twelve years ago,
the Tower fell from the sky, head first.
lines.village_card.03:
Graves lined the foot of the Tower.
Blades stood planted among the crosses.
lines.village_graves.01:
Before he went in, he passed the graves.
Planted above them, the Tower itself
looked like one enormous blade.
lines.village_chief.01:
…Another one has come. ……That blade…
…No. I was mistaken.
Old eyes see things that aren't there.
lines.village_chief.02: Many graves here have swords in them.
lines.village_chief.03:
For those who went into the Tower.
In Gabu, a warrior's grave
bears the blade he carried.
lines.village_chief.04:
People don't come back.
The Tower spits out only their blades.
lines.village_chief.05:
…*mumble*… Blades?
Smells like blades… how many…
lines.village_chief.06: It's a grave. Don't eat it.
lines.village_chief.07:
My boy Ren went in too.
Said he'd be back before sundown.
lines.village_chief.08:
I dig the graves myself.
Only one stands empty.
…Its owner hasn't come yet.
lines.village_chief.09:
I won't ask your name.
I'd only have to carve it in stone.
When you come back, I'll ask then.
lines.village_chief.10:
If anyone in the Tower
speaks sweet words to you,
ask the price first.
lines.village_chief.11: I always ask the price first.
lines.ch0_start.01:
I climbed, yet it smells of earth.
Forest below, leaves falling from above.
…This Tower's upside down.
lines.ch0_start.02:
In the Tower, up is where the Tower says.
…Still, this smell…
where have I smelled it before?
lines.trait_guardian.01:
Its shield is up when the fight opens,
and back up fast whenever it drops.
Plain hits: 1. Earnest cuts: a quarter.
lines.trait_guardian.02:
An earnest cut on a shield is a waste.
I'll read the numbers and reorder.
lines.mech_rune.01:
The Tower's glyph! Once swallowed,
it's carved into your body for good.
lines.mech_rune.02:
One point of attack…
Won't even notice it.
lines.mech_rune.03:
Each floor sets three of the same kind.
One point pays off three times.
Defense and health come round in turn.
lines.mech_levelup.01:
Kahaha! I shared a bit of what I ate.
As the contract says.
lines.mech_levelup.02:
The more you grow, the cheaper the rest.
Buy the pricey ones later,
and eat while you can.
lines.mech_spare_key.01: A spare key. If unused, it carries over.
lines.mech_nokey.01: No key. Every zone holds the next key.
lines.mech_fatal.01:
A red X instead of a number.
That's not a price. It's your life.
lines.mech_fatal.02:
What you have now can't buy this.
Come back grown, or after a potion,
or buy a different one first.
lines.mech_overflow.03:
Step on potions after you fight.
Only an empty bowl keeps what's poured.
lines.mech_vault.01:
A fourth door. Not a path, but a vault.
The Tower's glyph lies inside.
lines.mech_vault.02:
A leftover key of its color opens it.
Keys carry over from floor to floor.
lines.mech_vault.03:
In the whole Tower, vaults outnumber
leftover keys. You can't open them all.
lines.mech_vault.04: The glyph changes from vault to vault.
lines.mech_vault.05:
Open it now, or save the key…
I'll do that math myself.
lines.mech_choice.01:
Potion or the Tower's glyph: pick one.
Take one, and the other vanishes.
lines.mech_choice.03: No. Only what you take first remains.
lines.mech_choice.04: …Then I'll take whatever I'm short on.
lines.mech_death.01:
…Just now, I was on my knees
and you were planted beside me.
Looked just like a grave.
lines.mech_death.02:
Grave? Nonsense.
Your life is mine.
You shall not die without my leave.
lines.mech_death.03:
I hauled you up to the threshold.
Body and floor, as when you entered.
lines.mech_death.04:
(From the menu, you can also
go back several floors.)
lines.f11_motto.01:
Kahaha! Let me teach you
how to survive the Tower, Two-bit.
lines.f11_motto.02:
The hungry get eaten,
and the full do the eating!
lines.f11_motto.05: Then you're the one getting eaten.
lines.f11_motto.06:
Th-this blade does the eating!
I'm only hungry, that's all!
lines.f16_nap.04:
Wh-what?!
I sleep with my eye open!
lines.f16_nap.05:
So you admit you were asleep.
…Sleepyhead.
lines.f16_nap.06:
Sleepyhead?!
Is that how you speak to a demon sword?!
lines.trait_beast.01:
This one reeks of beast.
If it falls under a tenth and lives,
it rises once, with four tenths back.
lines.trait_beast.02: And that's already in the number?
lines.trait_beast.03:
Naturally. My eye misses nothing.
Save Smash for just above a tenth:
one blow, and it never rises.
lines.boss0_intro.03:
No mere monster
could know me.
lines.boss0_intro.04:
…The sun… is setting…
…I have to go…
lines.boss0_intro.06:
It's floating right over its head.
Kahaha! Supper time, Two-bit!
lines.boss0_defeat.01:
…Before sundown…
I said… I'd go home…
lines.boss0_defeat.02:
Where the wolf fell,
the ring from its neck rolled free.
lines.boss0_defeat.04: You said no mere monster could know you.
lines.boss0_defeat.05:
…It wasn't a monster.
The Tower molds the fallen into monsters
and stands them up as gatekeepers.
lines.boss0_defeat.08:
……Two-bit adventurer.
Have you anywhere to go back to
before sundown?
lines.mech_warp.03: Ren… That was the chief's son.
lines.mech_warp.04:
……Any floor you've already been to,
this ring takes you to its threshold.
lines.mech_warp.05:
Left a vault unopened down below?
Go back with your leftover keys.
lines.ch1_start.01:
…Water's dripping from above.
And we're heading underground.
lines.ch1_start.02:
Ptoo, ptoo! Water on my blade!
If I rust, you're polishing me, Two-bit.
lines.ch1_start.03:
And as I told you:
in the Tower, up is
where the Tower says.
lines.ch1_start.04:
Then which way
has the Tower decided is up?
lines.trait_knight.01:
It cuts twice while others cut once.
But every blow is light.
lines.trait_knight.02:
So one point of defense blocks twice.
Defense runes will earn their keep here.
lines.f27_sleeptalk.04: Wh-what?! A dream! Just a dream!
lines.f27_sleeptalk.05:
Sleepyhead.
Doors, even in your dreams?
lines.f27_sleeptalk.06:
Silence!
My dreams are my own affair!
lines.f31_trust.02:
…You haven't been
checking the numbers lately.
lines.f31_trust.05:
Kahaha! Naturally!
My eye misses nothing!
lines.f31_trust.06:
…Hmph. Look now and then anyway.
A long way yet.
lines.f35_suspect.01:
Five more floors up
and the waterway ends. Then it gets hot.
lines.f35_suspect.02:
Brace yourself, two-bit adventurer.
This blade does not melt. You do.
lines.f35_suspect.05: (…Yet it acted like the Tower was news.)
lines.boss1_intro.01:
For the record.
One intruder. One sword with an eye.
lines.boss1_intro.03:
…A goblin this time.
This one was a person too, right?
lines.boss1_intro.04:
…Yes. Like the wolf,
the Tower remade him.
lines.boss1_intro.05:
Bram…
The name signed on the request slip.
lines.boss1_intro.06:
That request is still posted?
…Of course. My report never came.
lines.boss1_intro.07:
Never turn your back on that sword.
…After the chief's son, it was me.
lines.boss1_defeat.01:
Never lowered… the shield. To the end.
So… here I stand.
lines.boss1_defeat.03:
……I've seen that shield before.
It was always turned toward me.
lines.boss1_defeat.10:
…Hmph. To the very end,
that one never trusted me. Fool.
lines.ch2_start.01:
The higher we go, the hotter it gets.
So we are heading underground.
lines.ch2_start.02:
We're underground,
yet the sun's highest here.
lines.ch2_start.04:
…This smell. I hate it.
No… I don't know.
lines.trait_magic.01:
Every hit it lands is in earnest.
But its body is frail.
Drag it out, and you die.
lines.trait_magic.02: Then I'd better end it early with Smash.
lines.trait_titan.01:
Every fifth hit it takes, it roars.
The roar hurts whoever struck it.
And it can take a beating.
lines.trait_titan.02: The harder each hit, the fewer roars.
lines.f45_forge.04:
Something about hunger.
What's that mean?
lines.f45_forge.05:
I don't know.
My mouth moved first.
lines.f50_leftovers.01:
…*mumble*… Something's odd lately.
My belly's filling up a bit.
lines.f50_leftovers.03:
Kahaha! That I'll grant you.
…But why did you come to this Tower?
lines.f50_leftovers.04:
I only take the requests
nobody else will.
lines.f50_leftovers.07:
Come to think of it,
you never even asked my name.
lines.f50_leftovers.10:
Kahaha! Don't like it? Grow bigger.
…A long way yet.
lines.f55_look.02: What was that look just now?
lines.f55_look.04: Last time you said you were filling up.
lines.f55_look.05:
…It's the furnace.
Pay it no mind.
lines.boss2_intro.03: Sounds like it's talking to you.
lines.boss2_intro.04:
So the ash speaks.
I can't make out a word.
lines.boss2_intro.06:
Expensive. Every hit is in earnest.
End it with Smash.
lines.boss2_defeat.06:
…What did that ash
say at the end?
lines.boss2_defeat.08:
…It said not to try melting me.
It tried, and ended up like that.
lines.boss2_defeat.12:
Ka… Kahaha…
I-I'm full. Off to sleep.
lines.ch3_start.01:
After the furnace, snow.
The sun's sinking, too.
Deeper than the fire, yet frozen.
lines.ch3_start.03:
Not sleepy?
Used to be, you'd be asleep by now.
lines.trait_immortal.01:
…Hateful things.
Only a fifth lands, unless it's earnest.
Same goes for Smash and Drain.
lines.trait_immortal.02:
I'll arrive with the breaths lined up.
Plan the order in the fights before.
lines.trait_assassin.01:
Hidden, it dodges anything not earnest.
An earnest cut makes it reveal itself.
Until then, even Smash hits air.
lines.trait_assassin.02: So who I cut first sets the price.
lines.f66_awake.03:
Then let me ask.
That name you mumbled in the aqueduct.
Who's Cedric?
lines.f66_awake.05:
…Don't fake it.
You said sleep won't come.
lines.f72_enough.03:
Enough what?
You always say 'a long way yet.'
lines.f76_nohome.01:
You…
said you had nowhere to go back to.
lines.boss3_intro.03:
You call my name. The second time.
The first was to beg me: open the door.
A Towerwarden. I kept the Throne's door.
lines.boss3_intro.04:
That sword was the Throne's master.
The Lock that held the Black Sun.
Monsters, its crumbs, gnaw at the Lock.
lines.boss3_intro.05:
Twelve years ago, I drew that sword,
the Tower fell, and I was bound here.
…Mercenary. What number are you?
lines.boss3_intro.08:
'Meeting me was your lucky day.'
…I heard those words too.
lines.boss3_intro.09:
There is a number over your head too.
That sword has watched it all along.
lines.boss3_intro.12:
The empty Throne calls its Lock back.
Only a soul bound to that sword may sit,
of its own accord. So it wins you over.
lines.boss3_intro.13:
'Only hunger can bind hunger.'
That sword was forged hungry.
It has never once been full.
lines.boss3_intro.14:
If that sword ever calls your name,
that is the end.
It names you only as it casts you away.
lines.boss3_intro.15:
Go back.
If you cannot, cut your way through.
lines.boss3_intro.16:
There's nowhere to go back to.
…So I'll cut my way through.
lines.boss3_defeat.01: …So it was in earnest. That sword.
lines.boss3_defeat.06:
You showed me every price.
All but one. Mine.
lines.boss3_defeat.08: …Enough to seat you on the Throne.
lines.boss3_defeat.09:
At first, I didn't know. Truly.
My mouth knew.
lines.boss3_defeat.11:
The furnace. When I ate that ash,
it all came back.
After that… I kept on, knowing.
lines.boss3_defeat.12:
Centuries. Alone, in the dark,
hungry, never once closing my eye.
…I just wanted to see the sky once.
lines.boss3_defeat.13:
Ren needed to get home.
Bram never trusted me. …He was right.
Elin tried to melt me down.
lines.boss3_defeat.14:
Contracts end only when one side breaks.
This blade does not break.
…So I let go.
lines.boss3_defeat.15:
'You shall not die without my leave.'
…So with your leave, I would.
lines.boss3_defeat.16:
Each time I let go, I called their name.
…Like a last farewell.
lines.boss3_defeat.19:
You said it has to be of my own accord.
So I just don't sit.
lines.ch4_card.01:
The Tower of legend
pierced a black sun and a crescent moon.
lines.ch4_card.02:
But what the Tower pierced
was no sun, and no moon.
lines.ch4_card.03:
It was a single eye,
and a curved blade.
lines.ch4_card.04:
The day the Lock was pulled,
the Tower fell head first.
lines.ch4_start.02:
The dust is being sucked upward.
Like something's breathing it in.
So the Tower's 'up' is the Black Sun.
lines.ch4_start.03:
My eye I'll lend you, as contracted.
My mouth… that I can't lend.
lines.ch4_start.04: The numbers are all I need.
lines.trait_armor.01:
So a shell, three tenths of its life,
soaks it all first. But no defense.
…Drain after the shell breaks.
lines.f85_honest.01:
Your numbers
never once lied to me.
lines.f85_honest.04: I'll keep showing you the numbers.
lines.f90_rule.01:
Pricey ones later.
Potions after fights; overflow's wasted.
Breaths carry over.
lines.f90_rule.04:
……Learn one more.
The Throne can never stand empty.
lines.f90_rule.05:
A soul bound to me must sit there
of its own accord, or the Tower
keeps sinking. The village goes first.
lines.f90_rule.07: And how does it get full?
lines.f90_rule.08:
Feed it. It fills with all you cut.
The ones you left on the floors below
are still there.
lines.f90_rule.10: So. When we reach the Throne?
lines.f90_rule.11: I'll tell you when we get there.
lines.f95_price.01:
……The Smith who forged me
left two sayings.
lines.f95_price.02:
'Only hunger can bind hunger.'
…The words my mouth remembered first.
lines.f95_price.03:
The other was this:
'Only fullness can end hunger.'
lines.f95_price.04:
I never
believed that one.
I'd never been full.
lines.f95_price.05: In the furnace, you said you were full.
lines.f95_price.07:
I did the math.
The price of getting here without you.
lines.f99_eve.01:
……Strange.
Getting sleepy in a place like this.
lines.f100_lesson.04:
The number on the one at the floor's end
changes with who you cut before it,
and in what order.
lines.f100_lesson.05: The breaths I count carry over.
lines.boss4_intro.03:
…So what it wants
is your eye.
lines.boss4_intro.04:
It was that thing's to begin with.
My eye is but a shard of it.
lines.boss4_intro.06:
Kahaha! Quiet, you.
I'm in the middle of a meal!
lines.boss4_intro.08:
Expensive.
…Buying it anyway.
Let's go, Two-bit!
lines.ending_choice.01:
Cutting it down won't kill hunger.
It's only lying low.
There. The Throne.
lines.ending_choice.05:
…Your plan
was to seat me there.
lines.ending_choice.07:
Contracts end only
when one side breaks.
This time, it's this blade that breaks.
lines.ending_choice.09:
I sleep.
I'm good at that, aren't I?
lines.ending_choice.10:
To my eye, everything had a price.
…Everything but you, now.
lines.ending_choice.13:
From the start.
You wrote it on the contract yourself.
lines.ending_seal.01:
In Gabu, on a warrior's grave,
they plant the blade he carried.
lines.ending_seal.02:
Damian
planted the blade he had carried.
lines.ending_seal.03:
Well done.
Worthy of my contractor.
lines.ending_seal.04:
This time I'll sleep with my eye open.
My specialty, isn't it?
lines.ending_seal.05:
When you die of old age, come here.
That's a contract.
lines.ending_seal.07:
…This time I'll call no one.
I'll just wait.
lines.ending_seal.09:
I'll haul you up one last time.
All the way out of the Tower.
lines.ending_seal.11:
The single eye slept, still open.
It never spoke a price again.
lines.epilogue_seal.01:
That night, the chief saw it:
the Tower falling upward,
back into its own sky.
lines.epilogue_seal.02:
The mercenary came back with the ring.
'Ren tried to come home, to the last.'
lines.epilogue_seal.03:
'I knew. What that blade was.
I knew, and still I sent you in.'
lines.epilogue_seal.04:
'I wanted someone to end it.
Even if the price was another's life.'
'I know.'
lines.epilogue_seal.06:
Only then did the chief ask his name.
'It's Damian.'
lines.epilogue_seal.07:
In the empty grave, Damian planted
the sword that hung at his own hip.
The demon sword's sky was too far away.
lines.epilogue_seal.08:
The black star in the night sky
blinks now and then,
like a sleepy eye.
lines.ending_hold.01:
…Let go!
This blade is all it takes!
lines.ending_hold.04:
……It's no use. I'm still hungry.
I can't swallow it like this.
The hungry… get eaten.
lines.ending_hold.07:
I know. Just like your plan.
I sit of my own accord. It'll take me.
…Not like I've anywhere to go back to.
lines.ending_hold.09:
Then I stay too.
It's in the contract, isn't it?
'Eternal companion.'
lines.ending_hold.12: We'll take turns sleeping. You first.
lines.ending_hold.13:
The Tower shook.
And toward the sky,
it began to fall.
lines.epilogue_hold.01:
From the cliff, the chief watched
the Tower return to its own sky,
the black sun run through once more.
lines.epilogue_hold.02:
Among the graves the Tower left behind,
a ring had been spat out.
The one he had given his son.
lines.epilogue_hold.03:
In the grave whose owner never came,
he buried the ring.
The name, he never got to ask.
lines.epilogue_hold.04:
On the guild board's old reward notice,
someone wrote: 'Completed.'
lines.epilogue_hold.05:
Children with sharp ears say
that at dusk, up in the sky,
two voices can be heard bickering.
lines.ending_dawn.01:
…Let go!
This blade is all it takes!
lines.ending_dawn.04:
I'm full.
For the first time in my life.
lines.ending_dawn.05: You said that day never comes.
lines.ending_dawn.06: …It came. You fed me, didn't you?
lines.ending_dawn.08:
…Kahaha!
Using my own lesson
against me, are you?
lines.ending_dawn.09:
Good. I'll swallow that thing.
The full do the eating.
lines.ending_dawn.10:
In a full bowl,
hunger can't stay.
It overflows, and goes to waste.
lines.ending_dawn.12:
…Called your name again.
Didn't cast you away, though.
Cedric had it wrong.
lines.ending_dawn.13:
What overflowed went to waste.
The Tower crumbled into motes of light.
lines.ending_dawn.15:
I can't see it.
There's nothing over your head
anymore.
lines.ending_dawn.16:
The contract is over.
The hungry blade has just broken.
Your soul, I return to you.
lines.ending_dawn.17:
Keep it.
I lose things anyway.
lines.epilogue_dawn.01: Morning came where the Tower had stood.
lines.epilogue_dawn.02:
For the first time in twelve years,
the sky over Gabu cleared.
lines.epilogue_dawn.03:
For the second time in its life,
the demon sword apologized.
'Old man. About Ren… I'm sorry.'
lines.epilogue_dawn.05:
The ring went back to Ren's father.
The chief filled in the empty grave,
and only then asked his name.
lines.epilogue_dawn.06:
Damian's report to the Kingdom
was a single line:
'Secret of the Tower: None.'
lines.epilogue_dawn.07:
He tore down the reward notice
and ripped it up himself.
lines.epilogue_dawn.08:
'Kahaha! Where to next, Damian?!'
'…How much does it pay?'
lines.credits.07: To you, who paid the price to the end.
lines.bark_basic_1.01: As usual. Just count the prices right.
lines.bark_basic_2.01: Numbers, then order. Same as always.
lines.bark_basic_3.01: Pricey ones later. Same math as ever.
lines.bark_stingy_1.01: Few potions here. Order is everything.
lines.bark_stingy_2.01: Few potions. Better time them right.
lines.bark_stingy_3.01: Scarce potions? Fight first, then step.
lines.bark_gate_1.01: Pricey one bars the way. Numbers first.
lines.bark_gate_2.01: So the way opens only past that one.
lines.bark_gate_3.01: Buy now, or grow first. That's the test.
lines.bark_plenty_1.01: Potions aplenty. Side paths pay off.
lines.bark_plenty_2.01: Plenty's no reason to stomp on them all.
lines.bark_plenty_3.01: Only an empty bowl keeps what's poured.
lines.bark_treasure_1.01: A glyph off the path. Count the detour.
lines.bark_treasure_2.01: One or the other. Take what you lack.
lines.bark_treasure_3.01: Potion or rune. I only get one.
lines.bark_death_1.01: Again. Change the order this time.
lines.bark_death_2.01: I tally the numbers. You set the order.
lines.bark_death_3.01: Get up. The price isn't paid yet.
lines.bark_death_5.01: The threshold. Count again from the top.

choices.ending_choice.seal: Plant the sword in the Throne
choices.ending_choice.hold: Don't let go of the sword

prologue_rewrites.900000:
An ordinary afternoon.
In front of the guild board.
prologue_rewrites.900001:
A rowdy guild. Only the board was quiet.
An old request hooked an adventurer.
prologue_rewrites.900003:
A giant tower fell from the sky.
Adventurers went. Nothing came to light.
prologue_rewrites.900004:
Now a cursed place, rife with monsters.
A royal reward for the Tower's secret.
prologue_rewrites.900005:
…… Rrrip.
He pocketed the request slip and left.
prologue_rewrites.900006:
Tch… I smell monsters.
No avoiding a fight, then.
prologue_rewrites.100013:
A talking sword…
Are you a monster?
prologue_rewrites.100014:
What? Don't lump me in with monsters!
You look like a common adventurer…
Ever heard of an Ego Sword?
prologue_rewrites.100015:
Ego… Sword?!
A sword with a mind of its own…
Don't tell me you're a demon sword?
prologue_rewrites.100016:
At last, you recognize me.
I am… the Ego Sword.
What your kind calls a demon sword!
prologue_rewrites.100018:
W-wait!
You're just going to leave?!
prologue_rewrites.100019:
Two-bit adventurer I may be, but still.
A demon sword without a drop of magic?
You expect me to buy that?
prologue_rewrites.100020:
Look at the state of me!
Abandoned so long, I can't recall when.
Damned monsters gnawed my magic away!
prologue_rewrites.100021: (Is that why the village is overrun…?)
prologue_rewrites.100023:
Sure, that was a fun story.
But I'm a busy man.
A magicless demon sword is dead weight.
prologue_rewrites.100024:
Hmph! Still don't believe me, eh?
Then here's a better story.
A demon sword's power comes by contract!
prologue_rewrites.100026:
Indeed. Meeting me was your lucky day.
Contract with me! I promise great power.
I'm sick to death of this forest, too.
prologue_rewrites.100027:
I'm headed for a ruined village.
Some unknown tower put a curse on it.
Just curiosity… but no backing out now.
prologue_rewrites.100028:
Kahaha! A tower teeming with monsters?
Let's go this instant!
prologue_rewrites.100031: Steady! Look at the numbers first.
prologue_rewrites.8:
[ Demon Sword Contract ]
The Contractor hereby enters a contract with the demon sword [Ego Sword].
By this contract, the Contractor gains the demon sword's great power,
and in return accepts that their soul and life belong to the demon sword.

◀The Sword's Power▶
The Contractor gains the right to wield the demon sword's power.
This power, however, is granted by the demon sword's will,
and its consequences are the Contractor's to bear.
◀Binding of the Soul▶
From the moment this contract is made, my soul belongs to the demon sword,
and my being becomes the demon sword's eternal companion.
◀The Price of Power▶
The Contractor may use the demon sword's power freely,
and in return offers the magic and weapons of monsters to the Ego Sword.
◀Irrevocable▶
This contract endures forever, until body and soul are destroyed.
◀Oath▶
The Contractor has read and understood every term of this contract,
and, signing of their own free will, shall faithfully fulfill them.
prologue_rewrites.7:
-Warning-

You sense danger beyond the door.
Will you enter?
prologue_rewrites.4029:
A demon sword with a mind of its own.
Grows by eating swords; lends its power.
Legendary, but usable only by contract.

chapters.name: Mossy Catacombs
chapters.subtitle: The Old Graves the Tower Swallowed

chapters.name: Collapsed Aqueduct
chapters.subtitle: Where the Sky's Rain Once Ran

chapters.name: Rift of the Throne
chapters.subtitle: The Rift the Black Sun Bores Into

mob_desc.0:0:
It spreads like moss wherever midday light falls through the cracks overhead.
It only bounces and rams like a ball, making it a good foe for learning to count prices.
The demon sword says there's nothing to chew on.
mob_desc.0:1:
It lures prey with a sweet scent that drifts among the falling leaves.
Charmed by it, you may cut whatever comes first, and your math gets tangled.
Let the numbers decide which one you pay for first.
mob_desc.0:2:
It flies low through the leaf shadows, pecking up anything that glints among the graves.
It beats up the dust with its wings, then drives its beak in.
No one knows what it swallowed to leave that blue glow spreading across its chest.
mob_desc.0:3:
A small spirit glowing green, alone in the earth-scented shade.
It gathers its light, then bristles the spines on its wingtips and darts out.
They say it woke on the night the Tower fell.
mob_desc.0:4:
In catacombs so hushed your ears feel plugged, it keeps glancing up at the light overhead, as if gauging where the sun is.
It crouches low, then lunges and bites in one move.
mob_desc.0:5:
A skittish goblin that thrusts its spear at every falling leaf.
It measures the distance, stabs, falls back, and stabs again.
The big ones draw in their spears, hunker down, and open the fight on guard.
mob_desc.0:6:
In the old graveyard the Tower swallowed lay the challengers who never made it past.
Their bones rise again, pull the blades from the old graves, and swing them.
Whose blades they were, only the smell of earth knows.
mob_desc.0:7:
It props its round shield in a leaf-strewn corner and crouches behind it.
It heaves the shield high, then slams it straight down.
The unusually large ones start the fight with the shield already up.
mob_desc.0:8:
Hunched under a coat of moss, at a glance it looks like a burial mound.
It never leaves its post, though it no longer knows whose orders it keeps.
Even when it strikes, its body does not budge.
mob_desc.0:9:
Under the light that filters through the leaves, a black bulk crouches with its wings folded.
When the blue flame crowning its head flickers, it spreads its wings and pounces.
Before its size scares you, look at the number first.
mob_desc.1:0:
It has swollen fat on the drops that fall from above.
Every time it rams, muddy water splashes.
When three appear together they have no special tricks, so the math is easiest.
mob_desc.1:1:
Under the dim light, its mango color has faded to mud, as if it drank Gabu's wells too.
It lies flat, then springs up and pounces.
The big ones pounce twice without pause, so the thicker your defense, the less it hurts.
mob_desc.1:2:
It circles above the ruined waterway, hiding its wingbeats in the sound of dripping water.
It shakes out its wet feathers as it dives in to peck.
The darker, bigger ones peck weakly but never let up.
mob_desc.1:3:
Its light bleeds into the damp air; it hangs dim, like a lantern in the mist.
Some draw their light in from the start and open the fight as a hard little kernel.
Against one curled up like that, even a critical hit deals only a quarter.
mob_desc.1:4:
Even through the reek of water, it picks out the smell of blood uncannily well.
It shakes its wet fur into a spray and lunges through it.
The biggest of the pack doesn't stop at one bite; it bites again and again.
mob_desc.1:5:
Dim light glistens on its waterlogged spearhead.
It stabs, pulls back, and stabs again.
Among them are some that open the fight with the shaft held crosswise as a guard.
mob_desc.1:6:
Drops patter into its empty eye sockets, and it doesn't so much as blink.
These are the bones of the fallen, raised back up by the Tower.
When three stand on one floor, they have no tricks and simply swing their blades.
mob_desc.1:7:
It holds its round shield against the falling water and stands firm, as if damming the channel.
The shield drops after taking one hit.
Don't waste a critical hit on that one hit.
mob_desc.1:8:
Slick as a wet boulder, with a few red dots blinking like eyes.
Keeping orders with no master, it won't budge even where the water seeps in.
When three of the same stand together, they simply squat and strike.
mob_desc.1:9:
The blue flame on its head doesn't go out, even as the drops fall.
It spreads its wings and pounces in a burst of spray.
Now and then, one opens the fight wrapped in its wings like a shield.
mob_desc.2:0:
It feeds on the rising sparks, and live coals smolder inside it.
When three appear together, they ram twice in the time it takes to bounce once.
Each hit is light, so the thicker your defense, the less it hurts.
mob_desc.2:1:
Cooked under firelight as high as noon, its mango color has turned to molten iron.
Its body scalds at a touch, so the longer you grapple, the more it hurts.
The big ones boil over every fifth hit they take, scalding whoever struck them.
mob_desc.2:2:
It soars up with the sparks, then plunges down on the hot wind.
Its half-scorched feathers give off an acrid smell.
When three stand on one floor, the beak comes in twice for every wingbeat.
mob_desc.2:3:
In the furnace heat its green glow burns orange, and it pops like a spark.
Some of them land every shot as a critical hit.
Those are frail, so don't drag it out. End it with Smash.
mob_desc.2:4:
In air that grows hotter the higher you climb, it pants with its tongue lolling out.
When three of the same stand together, they bite, let go, and bite again without pause.
Each bite is weak, so the thicker your defense, the longer you last.
mob_desc.2:5:
It heats its spearhead in the sparks and stabs while it still glows red.
The unusually large ones shriek and swing their shaft back at you every fifth hit they take.
The harder each hit, the less of that racket you hear.
mob_desc.2:6:
Ash has settled in every joint, and it sheds a flurry of it with each move.
It cuts with wide swings of a scorched blade.
Some of them land every swing as a critical hit. End those early with Smash.
mob_desc.2:7:
The rim of its heated shield glows red in the firelight.
As it raises the shield and slams it down, a gust of hot air hits your face first.
The big ones strike back with their shield every fifth hit they take.
mob_desc.2:8:
Hunched like a lump of charcoal among the rising sparks, only its red eyes blink.
Its masterless orders hold, even before this fire.
Now and then one lands every blow as a critical hit; the longer the fight, the more it hurts.
mob_desc.2:9:
Though the firelight hangs high as noon, the shadow under its wings stays deep.
The blue flame on its head crackles against the furnace fire.
On floors where they come in threes, they strike twice, surprisingly quick for their size.
mob_desc.3:0:
Snowed on under the evening light, its surface has set into a thin crust of ice.
When three appear together, anything but a critical hit deals only a fifth.
Your critical count carries over between fights, so line it up through the order of the fights before.
mob_desc.3:1:
Robbed of its warmth by the snow, even its sweet scent has frozen.
The big ones seem about to collapse, then pull themselves together and rise once more.
That rise is already counted in the expected damage.
mob_desc.3:2:
In the falling snow, only its black feathers stand out. The snow swallows the sound of its wings.
Some hide in the blizzard and let everything but critical hits slip past.
mob_desc.3:3:
Snow falls in the evening gloom, and its green light, trapped in frost, flickers faintly.
When three stand on one floor, their frozen light makes them sluggish, but anything short of a critical hit only scratches the surface.
mob_desc.3:4:
The evening sun lies low, and its crouching shadow stretches long.
The biggest of the pack, when about to fall, howls and rises once more.
That too is counted in the expected damage.
mob_desc.3:5:
Its hands have frozen to the shaft in the snow; it stands there, unable to let go.
Among them are some that hide in the snow, and no blade touches them until they take a critical hit.
mob_desc.3:6:
Frost sits white on every joint, and ice has filled in the breaks.
When three of the same stand together, almost nothing but critical hits gets through.
No one knows whose bones these are.
mob_desc.3:7:
Snow piles thick on its frozen shield; from afar it looks like a small snow-covered grave.
The big ones seem about to fall, then lean on their shield and rise once more.
Save Smash and finish it in one blow from just above 10% HP, and it can't get up.
mob_desc.3:8:
Where even warmth was eaten, it lies smothered in snow, yet its red eyes alone have not cooled.
Keeping its masterless orders, it buries itself in the snow.
Now and then one hides away entirely, and anything but a critical hit swings at empty air.
mob_desc.3:9:
Where the evening sun lies long, the shadow of its wings covers the floor.
On floors where they come in threes, their wingbeats are sluggish, but they barely feel anything but critical hits.
Line up your critical count in the fights before, then take it on.
mob_desc.4:0:
In the violet dusk, its body stretches upward, drawn after the rising dust.
When three appear together, they wear shells of caked dust.
The shell takes everything first, but once it cracks, the inside is soft.
mob_desc.4:1:
All the dust is drawn upward, toward the black sun.
This one keeps leaning that way too, as if that were where it broke off from.
The big ones hide in the dust and let everything but critical hits slip past.
mob_desc.4:2:
In a rift where dust is sucked upward, it flaps without rest, as if it would float away the moment its wings stopped.
Some shriek every fifth hit they take and peck back at whoever struck them.
That cry is already counted in the expected damage.
mob_desc.4:3:
Stained by the violet evening, its green glow has darkened like a bruise.
When three stand on one floor, they pack the dust into shells.
Use Drain after the shell breaks. What the shell absorbs never comes back as blood.
mob_desc.4:4:
It lifts its head and howls at the rising dust, but the rift swallows the sound and nothing comes back.
The unusually large ones melt into the shadows and dodge everything but critical hits.
Who you cut first, before it, sets its price.
mob_desc.4:5:
Its spearhead always points up, toward the black sun where the dust is drawn.
When three of the same stand together, they wear shells of dust.
The shell takes everything first, but once it breaks, nothing is left to guard them.
mob_desc.4:6:
The dusk stains its bones violet, and the dust shed from its joints scatters upward.
Among them are some that bring their blade down in return every fifth hit they take.
The harder each hit, the less of that blade you take.
mob_desc.4:7:
The dust on its shield flows up instead of sliding off.
On floors where they come in threes, a shell takes the blows instead of the shield.
It has no skill at blocking, so once the shell breaks, it's soft.
mob_desc.4:8:
Hunched at the edge of the rift the black sun bores into, it stares only upward with red eyes.
Its masterless orders were left by the Towerwardens who once guarded the Throne.
The big ones hide in the dust, and no blade touches them until they take a critical hit.
mob_desc.4:9:
Crawling up from deep in the rift, it swallows the rising dust with the blue flame on its head.
A beast whose hunger never fades, whatever it eats.
Now and then one roars every fifth hit it takes, paying back whoever struck it.

bosses.name: Wolf of the Catacombs
bosses.title: The One Who Waits for Dusk
bosses.desc:
A wolf that never leaves the door at the catacombs' end. Something hangs around its neck.
Once, when its HP drops to 10% or less, it recovers 40% of its max HP and rises again. That is already counted in the expected damage.

bosses.name: Shieldbearer of the Aqueduct
bosses.title: The Shield Never Lowered
bosses.desc:
A shieldbearer blocking the collapsed aqueduct with its own body.
It starts the fight with its shield up, and raises it again soon after it drops.

bosses.name: Sentinel of Ash
bosses.title: The Voice That Did Not Burn
bosses.desc:
An ashen sentinel guarding the furnace. Its words crumble like ash, leaving only fragments.
Every attack is a critical hit.

bosses.name: The Frozen Knight
bosses.title: Warden of the Last Door
bosses.desc:
A knight guarding the last door before the Throne. Frost lies thick on every joint.
Anything but a critical hit deals only 20%, so it barely gets hurt.

bosses.name: The Black Sun
bosses.title: Endless Hunger
bosses.desc:
The hunger the Tower once pierced and held fast. Black-winged and crowned with blue flame, it has claimed the bottom of the rift.
Every fifth hit it takes, it roars and pays back whoever struck it. That is already counted in the expected damage.

traits.name: None
traits.desc:
No special ability.
Having no tricks makes it handy for shifting your critical count.

traits.name: Beast
traits.desc:
Once, if its HP drops to 10% or less while it still lives, it recovers 40% of its max HP.
The recovery is already counted in the expected damage.
Save Smash. Finish it with one Smash from just above 10% HP, and it can't rise.

traits.name: Magic
traits.desc:
Every attack is a critical hit. In exchange, its HP is low.
The longer the fight, the more it hurts. End it early with Smash.

traits.name: Guardian
traits.desc:
Starts the fight with its shield up, and its guard gauge fills quickly.
The shield drops after taking one hit. Against it, non-critical hits deal 1 and critical hits only a quarter.
Use the fights before to shift your critical count so your critical hit doesn't land on the shield.

traits.name: Immortal
traits.desc:
Takes only 20% from non-critical hits. Smash and Drain deal only 20% too.
Your critical count carries over between fights. Use the fights before to arrive with it lined up.

traits.name: Swordsman
traits.desc:
Attacks twice as fast, but each hit is light.
Because it hits so often, each point of defense cuts its damage twice. Defense runes are worth double.

traits.name: Titan
traits.desc:
Every fifth hit it takes, it roars, returning 20% of its normal attack to whoever struck it. Lots of HP.
The roar is already counted in the expected damage.
The harder each hit, the fewer hits to finish it, and the fewer roars you hear.

traits.name: Assassin
traits.desc:
While hidden, it dodges every non-critical hit. Smash and Drain miss too.
A critical hit reveals it, and after that every attack lands.
Your critical count carries over between fights. Who you cut first sets the price.

traits.name: Armor
traits.desc:
A shell worth 30% of its max HP absorbs all damage first. Its defense is 0.
Use Drain after breaking the shell. What the shell absorbs never comes back as blood.

monster_book.name: Monster Manual
monster_book.desc:
A book that copies down what the demon sword's eye recognizes.
The mind may forget, but the eye knows what shares its root.
Shows this floor's monsters and the price of each fight at a glance.

warp_ring.name: Warpstone Ring
warp_ring.desc:
A ring engraved inside: 'To Ren. Before sundown.'
It takes you straight back to the threshold of any floor you've visited, the spot where you first set foot.

key.name: Key
key.desc:
Opens one door of the same color, then vanishes.
Unused keys carry over between floors, and open vault doors too.

potion.name: Potion
potion.desc:
Drunk the moment you step on it, restoring a portion of your max HP. It can't be carried.
Whatever overflows goes to waste, so step on it after you fight.

rune.name: Rune
rune.desc:
The Tower's glyph. The moment you swallow it, it's carved into your body.
Permanently raises one of: ATK +1, DEF +1, or max HP +5. One on every floor, and more inside vaults.
